# mnml-cms

> A small schema-driven CMS that lives inside your Next.js site.

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/index.md -->

# mnml-cms

A small CMS that lives inside your Next.js site.

- **One config file** defines your content.
- **The admin** is a route in your app (`/admin`).
- **Entries** live in your Postgres, one JSON table. No migrations when the model changes.

- **AI agents** edit content through the built-in MCP server. Drafts only; an editor approves deletes. ([Agents](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/agents.md))
- **Docs for agents:** every page is Markdown at its URL plus `.md`, and the MCP `docs` tool links to them. ([Help your AI agent](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/getting-started.md#help-your-ai-agent))

Needs Next 16+ (App Router), React 19+ and Tailwind v4.

Start: [Getting started](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/getting-started.md). Full app: [`example/`](https://github.com/mbuguanewton/mnml-cms/tree/main/example).

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

## Where files go

```text
mnml.config.ts        content model (plain data)
src/mnml/
  index.ts            createCms(...), exports `cms`
  editor.tsx          rich-text editor setup, shared with the site
  editor-client.tsx   the editor for the admin ('use client')
  ui.tsx              your own admin controls
```

Only `index.ts` is needed to start. Add the rest when you use them (see [Custom admin UI](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/custom-admin-ui.md) and [Editor](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/editor.md)).

## Help your AI agent

Add to your `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`:

```md
Read node_modules/@n3wtou/mnml-cms/AGENTS.md before changing anything that uses mnml-cms.
```

- Every docs page is Markdown at its URL plus `.md`, e.g. [/agents.md](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/agents.md). Index: [llms.txt](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/llms.txt). Everything: [llms-full.txt](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/llms-full.txt).
- With the [MCP server](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/agents.md) on, the `docs` tool hands agents the right `.md` links.

## Install

```sh
pnpm add @n3wtou/mnml-cms drizzle-orm
```

## Environment variables

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Postgres connection string |
| `ADMIN_PASSWORD` | The shared admin password |
| `ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET` | Signs the session cookie. 32+ random characters. |
| `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` | Vercel Blob token, for image uploads only ([Image storage](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/image-storage.md)) |

## 1. Define your content

Plain data, safe to import anywhere.

```ts filename="mnml.config.ts"
import { collection, config, fields, singleton } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms';

export default config({
  settings: singleton({ label: 'Settings', preview: '/', fields: { name: fields.text('Name', { required: true }) } }),
  posts: collection({
    label: 'Posts',
    titleField: 'title',
    basePath: '/blog', // served at /blog/<slug>
    preview: true, // live preview next to the editor
    fields: {
      title: fields.text('Title', { required: true }),
      date: fields.date('Date'),
      content: fields.richtext('Content'),
    },
  }),
});
```

## 2. Create the CMS

Server only. Keep everything that sets up the CMS in one `src/mnml/` folder: `index.ts` exports `cms`, and the files you add later sit beside it, named for what they are (`editor.tsx`, `editor-client.tsx`, `ui.tsx`, a custom node's `youtube.ts`). Import it as `@/mnml`.

```ts filename="src/mnml/index.ts"
import { createCms, neonDatabase, vercelBlobMedia } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/next';
import config from '../../mnml.config';

export const cms = createCms(config, {
  database: neonDatabase(process.env.DATABASE_URL), // or any Drizzle Postgres database
  auth: { password: process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD, secret: process.env.ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET },
  media: vercelBlobMedia(), // optional
});
```

## 3. Mount the admin

```ts filename="app/admin/[[...path]]/page.tsx"
import { cms } from '@/mnml';
export default cms.AdminPage;
```

```ts filename="app/api/mnml/[...route]/route.ts"
import { cms } from '@/mnml';
export const { GET, POST } = cms.handlers;
```

```ts filename="proxy.ts"
import { adminProxy } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/proxy';
export const proxy = adminProxy({ secret: process.env.ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET });
export const config = { matcher: ['/admin', '/admin/:path*'] };
```

Put the site's header and footer in a route group layout (e.g. `app/(site)/layout.tsx`) to keep them out of the admin.

## 4. Add the styles

In your global CSS:

```css
@import "@n3wtou/mnml-cms/styles.css";
```

Restyle the admin by overriding `--mnml-*` variables (see `styles.css`).

## 5. Create the table

Point drizzle-kit at the package's schema:

```ts filename="drizzle.config.ts"
export default defineConfig({ dialect: 'postgresql', schema: './node_modules/@n3wtou/mnml-cms/dist/server/content/db.js', dbCredentials: { url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! } });
```

Run `drizzle-kit push`. Scripts import the same table from `@n3wtou/mnml-cms/schema`.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/agents.md -->

# Agents (MCP)

Let AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Zed) edit your content. The CMS has a built-in MCP server. Agents use the same checks as the admin.

- Agents write drafts. Nothing goes live until `publish`.
- Agents can't delete or discard alone. An editor approves in the admin.
- Each agent has its own token. The token's scopes decide what it can do.

Keep the setup in your `src/mnml/` folder, beside the rest of the CMS wiring ([Getting started](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/getting-started.md#where-files-go)): the `mcp` option below goes in `src/mnml/index.ts`.

## Set up

1. Make a token (32+ random characters):

   ```sh
   openssl rand -hex 32
   ```

2. Put it in your env: `.env.local` locally, your host's settings in production.

   ```sh
   MNML_AGENT_TOKEN=…
   ```

3. Turn on the server:

   ```ts filename="src/mnml/index.ts"
   export const cms = createCms(config, {
     // …
     mcp: {
       tokens: [{ name: 'claude', token: process.env.MNML_AGENT_TOKEN, scopes: ['read', 'draft'] }],
     },
   });
   ```

Done. The server lives at `<apiPath>/mcp`, e.g. `https://your-site.com/api/mnml/mcp`. Your route file (`export const { GET, POST } = cms.handlers`) already serves it.

- No token set (and no `adminTokens`): the route is off (404).
- Token under 32 characters: ignored, with a warning in the log.

## Tokens

The agent sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It must match the value in your site's env exactly.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `token` | The secret, e.g. `process.env.MNML_AGENT_TOKEN`. Unset: ignored. |
| `name` | Shown as `change.by` in `onChange`, and on approval requests. Default `'agent'`. |
| `scopes` | What the token can do. Default `['read', 'draft']`. |
| `collections` | Only these keys, e.g. `['posts']`. Default: all. |

One token per agent or person. Then each has its own scopes and name, and you can revoke one alone. To rotate, change the value on the site and in the agent.

```ts
mcp: {
  tokens: [
    { name: 'newton', token: process.env.MNML_TOKEN_NEWTON, scopes: ['read', 'draft', 'publish'] },
    { name: 'blog-bot', token: process.env.MNML_TOKEN_BOT, collections: ['posts'] },
  ],
},
```

### Tokens from the admin

Let editors make tokens in the admin instead of env vars:

```ts
mcp: { adminTokens: true },
```

- **Agent access** appears in the sidebar (under Tools).
- Create: name, scopes (default `read` + `draft`), content (default all). The token (`mnml_…`) shows **once**, with a ready `claude mcp add` command. Copy it then.
- Stored as a SHA-256 hash in the entries table. No migration.
- The list shows each token's scopes, content, created and last used (updated at most once a minute).
- **Revoke** cuts access on the agent's next request.
- Config tokens still work alongside, and show in the list as "from config". Names are unique across both.
- **Revoke** on a config token only explains what to do: remove it from the `mcp.tokens` option (or its environment variable) and redeploy. It keeps working until then, since it lives in your config, not in the database.

### Scopes

| Scope | Can | Tools |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read` | Read schema and entries, drafts too | `get_schema`, `list_entries`, `get_entry`, `search`, `search_content`, `validate_entry`, `diff_entry`, `get_preview_url` |
| `draft` | Create entries, save drafts, import images | `create_entry`, `update_entry`, `upload_media_from_url` |
| `publish` | Go live, go offline, ask to discard | `publish`, `unpublish`, `discard_draft` |
| `delete` | Ask to delete | `delete_entry` |

- Scopes don't include each other. List each one you want.
- Agents only see tools they have scopes for. Others fail with the missing scope's name.
- A singleton without `drafts: true` has no draft: saving it goes live. So `update_entry` on it needs `publish` too.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get_schema` | All content the token can use. Each field as JSON Schema: type, required, options, limits. Call first. |
| `list_entries` | A collection's entries: `status`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `hasDraftChanges`. Filter, sort, page. |
| `get_entry` | One entry, latest version, drafts included. Shows a waiting approval request. Rich text as JSON or Markdown. |
| `search` | Find text in entries, rich text too. Latest versions, drafts included. |
| `search_content` | Best passages from published content, by meaning and words. Only with [`search`](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/search.md) on. |
| `validate_entry` | Check data, save nothing. Returns errors per field. |
| `diff_entry` | Fields where the draft differs from live. |
| `get_preview_url` | Link to see the draft on your site. Editors only. |
| `create_entry` | New collection entry, as a draft. Slug comes from the title unless given. Missing fields get their default. |
| `update_entry` | Change some fields. The rest stay. |
| `upload_media_from_url` | Copy an https image (4 MB max) into your storage. Returns a value for an `image` field. |
| `publish` | Make the latest version live. |
| `unpublish` | Take an entry off the site. It becomes a draft. |
| `discard_draft` | Ask to throw away unpublished changes. |
| `delete_entry` | Ask to delete an entry. |

- Bad data returns errors per field, same checks as the admin.
- Unknown field names fail. They are never dropped silently.

### Rich text

Agents write rich text as Markdown. The server turns it into Tiptap JSON.

```json
{ "title": "Hello", "content": "## Intro\n\nSome **bold** text and a [link](https://x.com).\n\n- one\n- two" }
```

- Works: headings, **bold**, *italic*, ~~strike~~, `code`, links, lists, quotes, code blocks, images, `---`.
- Tables and raw HTML: refused with a field error. Send Tiptap JSON (`{ "type": "doc", "content": [...] }`) for those.
- References and your own editor nodes: Tiptap JSON only.
- Works in nested fields too (groups, arrays, blocks).

To read rich text as Markdown, pass `richText: 'markdown'` to `get_entry` or `list_entries`. It's shorter than JSON. Nodes Markdown can't show come out as `<!-- mnml:<type> -->`, and the result has `lossy: true`. Don't write that Markdown back, or those nodes are lost.

## Drafts

Same rules as [Drafts and publishing](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/drafts-and-publishing.md):

- `create_entry`: a draft. 404 on the site.
- `update_entry` on a published entry: live version stays. The edit waits beside it (orange dot in the admin).
- `publish`: live, and the site revalidates.

`get_preview_url` gives `<apiPath>/preview/open?key=…&slug=…`. It opens the page in Draft Mode, only for editors signed in to the admin. Everyone else goes to login.

## Approval

`delete_entry` and `discard_draft` change nothing. They create a request and return `status: 'awaiting_approval'` plus `approveUrl` (the entry's admin page).

- The list shows **Awaiting approval**.
- The entry page shows the request with **Reject** and **Approve**.
- Discard is refused if the draft changed after the request.
- One request per entry. A new one replaces the old.
- Publishing the draft drops a discard request.

`get_entry` returns a waiting request as `awaitingApproval`.

## Connect an agent

Locally, use `http://localhost:3000/api/mnml/mcp`. The header must be `Authorization`, value `Bearer <token>`.

### Claude Code

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http mnml https://your-site.com/api/mnml/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $MNML_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

Or commit `.mcp.json` so your whole team gets it. The token comes from each person's env, never from git:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mnml": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://your-site.com/api/mnml/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${MNML_AGENT_TOKEN}" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Zed

In `settings.json`:

```json
"context_servers": {
  "mnml": {
    "url": "https://your-site.com/api/mnml/mcp",
    "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <token>" }
  }
}
```

### Cursor

In `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. It holds the token, so keep it out of git.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mnml": {
      "url": "https://your-site.com/api/mnml/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <token>" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude connectors

Not yet. Connectors in claude.ai and the Claude apps need OAuth, and the server doesn't support it yet. Use a client that can send a header.

## Security

- Tokens live in env vars. Never commit them.
- Give the fewest scopes. `['read', 'draft']` can't change the live site.
- Limit with `collections` when you can.
- `upload_media_from_url` only fetches public https hosts. Private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused, on every redirect too.
- Browser requests from other sites are refused, same as the admin.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields.md -->

# Field types

Every field takes `{ required, help }`.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `text`, `textarea` | `string` |
| `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `url` | `string \| null` |
| `datetime` | `string \| null`, UTC (`2026-11-18T14:30:00.000Z`). Edited in local time. |
| `number(label, { min, max, step })` | `number \| null` |
| `boolean` | `boolean`, default `false` |
| `select(label, ['a', 'b'] as const)` | `'a' \| 'b' \| null`. Options can have [labels](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/select-labels.md). |
| `reference(label, 'authors')` | `string \| null`: a published entry's slug. Read with `cms.getEntry`. |
| `references(label, 'posts', { min, max })` | `string[]`: published slugs, in order. Read with `cms.getEntries`. |
| `image` | `{ url, alt, focalX?, focalY? } \| null`. [Focal point](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/focal-point.md) optional. In the admin: an empty field is a drop zone (drop, click or browse); a filled one is a preview with an icon toolbar (Replace, Choose from uploads, Focal point, Remove) and a `filename · width×height` chip. |
| `richtext` | Tiptap JSON. Render with `<RichText>`. |
| `tags` | `string[]` |
| `array(label, fields, { itemLabel, min, max })` | Repeatable list of `fields` |
| `group(label, fields)` | Nested object, one form section: `page.hero.headline` |
| `blocks(label, { hero: block('Hero', fields), … }, { itemLabel, min, max })` | Sections of different [blocks](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/blocks.md): `{ kind: 'hero', …fields }[]` |
| `seo(label?)` | `group` of `title`, `description`, `image` ([SEO](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/seo.md)) |

## Picking entries

`reference` and `references` use a search box: filter by title or slug, pick with ↓/↑ + Enter or a click.

- `reference`: shows the pick, with a clear (×) button.
- `references`: shows the picks. [Drag to reorder](#reordering-lists), remove, add up to `max`.

```ts
related: fields.references('Related posts', 'posts', { max: 3 }),
authors: fields.references('Authors', 'authors', { required: true }),
```

`references` validation:

- Slugs trimmed. Blanks and repeats dropped.
- Then `min` / `max`. `required` = at least one.
- An entry unpublished later stays, marked "(unavailable)". Readers skip it.

### Create new

Next to the search box, **Create new** opens a panel on the right with the target collection's form. Make the entry without leaving the one you're editing.

- **Publish** creates it live and picks it. **Save draft** creates a draft and picks it, shown as "(draft)". The picker doesn't list drafts, and readers skip them, until you publish.
- Slug follows the title until you edit it. Errors show per field and keep the panel open.
- Close or Cancel asks first if you typed anything.
- A reference field inside the panel has its own **Create new**.
- Turn it off per field: `fields.reference('Author', 'authors', { createNew: false })`.

## Reordering lists

`array`, `blocks` and `references` rows have a grip on the left. Drag it to move the row.

- Mouse, touch and pen. A line shows where the row will drop. Letting go away from the list, or pressing Escape, cancels.
- Keyboard: focus the grip, then ↑ / ↓ move the row one place, Home and End to the top or bottom. Focus stays on the row, and a screen reader hears the new position.
- An open row stays open while it moves, and a row's validation errors move with it (also when a row is removed). Order is the order readers get.

## Groups become tabs

Groups add tabs above the form: **All fields**, **General** (fields outside groups), one per group.

A page with fixed sections: one singleton, a group per section. Editors add pages: a collection.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/limits.md -->

# Limits

`array`, `blocks`, `references` take `min` / `max` item counts.

```ts
links: fields.array('Links', { label: fields.text('Label'), url: fields.url('URL') }, { max: 4 }),
sections: fields.blocks('Sections', { hero, text }, { min: 1 }),
```

- `required` = at least one.
- Out of range: save fails with a field error ("Add at least 1 item"); autosave pauses.
- At `max`, Add is disabled with a reason.
- Fields hidden by `showIf` aren't checked.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/blocks.md -->

# Blocks

`blocks`: a page of different kinds of sections, each kind with its own fields.

```ts
sections: fields.blocks('Sections', {
  hero: block('Hero', { title: fields.text('Title'), image: fields.image('Image') }),
  posts: block('Posts', { count: fields.number('How many') }),
  divider: block('Divider', {}),
}),
```

## In the admin

- "Add section" opens the block list (search box above eight blocks).
- Editors see only the picked block's fields.
- `block(label, fields, { description })`: one-line hint in the list.
- `fields.blocks(…, { addLabel })`: renames the button.
- Drag a section by its grip to reorder (or focus the grip and use the arrow keys). See [Reordering lists](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields.md#reordering-lists).

## Reading

Each item stores its block key as `kind`. Check it to narrow the type: after `section.kind === 'hero'`, `section.image` is typed.

- `kind` is reserved: no block field may be named `kind`.
- A `kind` no longer in the config is dropped on read, and gone from the entry on its next save.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/select-labels.md -->

# Select labels

An option is a value, or a value with a label (shown in the admin). Mix freely.

```ts
category: fields.select('Category', ['news', { value: 'guide', label: 'How-to guide' }] as const), // 'news' | 'guide' | null
```

- Types come from the values.
- Entries, `default`, `showIf`, validation: values, not labels.
- A repeated value throws at config load.

Label on your site: `selectLabel` with the field from your config:

```ts
selectLabel(config.posts.fields.category, post.category);
```

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/dates-and-times.md -->

# Dates and times

| Field | Stores |
| --- | --- |
| `date` | A day (`YYYY-MM-DD`), no time zone |
| `datetime` | A moment in UTC, one format: `2026-11-18T14:30:00.000Z` |

## In the admin

- Type the date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. A day that doesn't exist (`2026-02-30`) is marked invalid and isn't saved.
- Or press the calendar button: arrows move by day and week, Home/End to the week's start and end, PageUp/PageDown by month (with Shift by year), Enter picks, Escape closes.
- The week starts on the browser locale's first day (Monday when unknown).
- `datetime`: one box, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm`. The calendar has a time row (hour and minute lists, type a number to jump) and a Done button; picking a day keeps the time and moves on to it. No native time popup.
- Touch screens get the browser's own picker.
- Your own picker: the `DatePicker` slot ([Custom admin UI](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/custom-admin-ui.md)).

`datetime`:

- One format, so `listEntries({ orderBy })` sorts by time.
- Admin edits it in the editor's time zone, named under the input.
- API values need `Z` or an offset (`2026-11-18T17:30+03:00`). Converted to UTC.
- `showIf` can test a value or `{ empty: true }`. `gt`, `lt`… are numbers only.

On your site, pick the display time zone. The server's is usually UTC.

```ts
new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', { dateStyle: 'long', timeStyle: 'short', timeZone: 'Europe/London' }).format(new Date(post.publishedAt));
```

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/focal-point.md -->

# Focal point

The part of an image to keep in frame when cropped.

## In the admin

- **Focal point** (crosshair button in the toolbar over the image) shows the whole image over the preview. Click the spot, or arrow keys (5%; 1% with Shift).
- **Reset** removes it. **X** (or Escape) closes focal mode. A new upload clears it.

## Stored value

`focalX`, `focalY`: 0–1 from left and top, 3 decimals. Both or neither. Old images read as before.

## On your site

`focalPosition(image)` returns CSS `object-position`: `"30% 40%"`, or `"50% 50%"` without a point.

```tsx
import { focalPosition } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms';

<img src={post.cover.url} alt={post.cover.alt} className="aspect-[16/9] object-cover" style={{ objectPosition: focalPosition(post.cover) }} />;
```

With `next/image`:

```tsx
<Image src={post.cover.url} alt={post.cover.alt} fill className="object-cover" style={{ objectPosition: focalPosition(post.cover) }} />;
```

By hand: `object-position: ${focalX * 100}% ${focalY * 100}%`, else `50% 50%`.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/default-values.md -->

# Default values

`default`: the starting value of a new entry, array item or block. A value, or a function returning one.

```ts
pageType: fields.select('Type', ['page', 'post'] as const, { default: 'page' }),
featured: fields.boolean('Featured', { default: false }),
date: fields.date('Date', { default: () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10) }), // today
count: fields.number('How many', { default: 3 }),
```

- **Type-checked.** A `select` default must be an option.
- **Create only:** new collection entry, never-saved singleton, new item, new block.
- **Never on read.** Missing stored fields read as empty.
- **Functions run when the form opens.** Later items in that form reuse that value (functions can't go to the browser).

Takes `default`: `text`, `textarea`, `number`, `boolean`, `select`, `date`, `datetime`, `url`, `reference`, `references`, `tags`. Groups: set defaults on their fields.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/conditional-fields.md -->

# Conditional fields

`showIf` shows a field only while its siblings match (fields next to it in the same entry, group, array item or block).

```ts
type: fields.select('Type', ['post', 'link'] as const),
url: fields.url('URL', { required: true, showIf: { type: 'link' } }),
badge: fields.text('Badge', { showIf: { type: ['link', 'video'], price: { gt: 0 } } }), // every key must match
```

## Conditions

| Condition | Sibling is |
| --- | --- |
| A value | equal |
| A list | any of them |
| `{ not: … }` | not the value (or none of the list) |
| `{ gt }`, `{ gte }`, `{ lt }`, `{ lte }` | a number in range |
| `{ empty: true \| false }` | empty, or not |

- Plain data, not functions, so the admin checks them while typing.
- Naming a non-sibling throws when the config loads.

## Hidden fields

- Not validated. A hidden `required` field never blocks a save.
- Value kept. Toggle back, text still there.
- Readers still return it. Check the same condition when rendering.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/derived-values.md -->

# Derived values

Extra values computed from an entry's own fields.

```ts
import { collection, derive, readingTime } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms';

posts: collection({
  // …
  derived: {
    readingTime: derive((post) => readingTime(post.content), { after: 'content' }),
    wordy: (post) => post.title.length > 60, // a plain function works too
  },
}),
```

- Run on every read. Never stored.
- Typed from the return type.
- Work in `orderBy` and `filter`.
- Pure functions of one entry. Can't share a field's name.
- Shown read-only in the form. `derive(fn, { after, label })` sets the field to show after (default: end) and the label.
- Rich text helpers: `plainText(doc)`, `readingTime(doc)`.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/fields/seo.md -->

# SEO

`fields.seo()`: a group of `title`, `description`, `image`. `seoMetadata(entry.seo, fallback)` makes Next.js `Metadata`; empties use `fallback`.

```ts
export const generateMetadata = async () => seoMetadata((await cms.getSingleton('home'))?.seo, { title: 'Home' });
```

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/reading-content.md -->

# Reading content

```tsx
import { cms } from '@/mnml';
import { RichText } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/rich-text';

const settings = await cms.getSingleton('settings');
const posts = await cms.listEntries('posts'); // [{ slug, entry, status, createdAt, updatedAt }]
const latest = await cms.listEntries('posts', { orderBy: 'date', order: 'desc', limit: 3 });
const post = await cms.getEntry('posts', slug);
const related = await cms.getEntries('posts', post.related); // [{ slug, entry }]
export const generateStaticParams = async () => (await cms.listSlugs('posts')).map((slug) => ({ slug }));

<RichText content={post.content} className="prose" />
```

Every result is typed from your config.

## A list page and a post page

```tsx
// app/(site)/blog/page.tsx
const posts = await cms.listEntries('posts', { orderBy: 'date', order: 'desc', limit: 10 });
posts.map(({ slug, entry }) => <Link key={slug} href={`/blog/${slug}`}>{entry.title}</Link>);
```

```tsx
// app/(site)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation';
import { RichText } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/rich-text';
import { seoMetadata } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms';
import { cms } from '@/mnml';

type Props = { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> };

export async function generateMetadata({ params }: Props) {
  const post = await cms.getEntry('posts', (await params).slug);
  return post ? seoMetadata(post.seo, { title: post.title }) : {};
}

export default async function Page({ params }: Props) {
  const post = await cms.getEntry('posts', (await params).slug);
  if (!post) notFound();
  return (
    <article>
      <h1>{post.title}</h1>
      {post.cover && <img src={post.cover.url} alt={post.cover.alt} />}
      <RichText content={post.content} />
    </article>
  );
}
```

## Static rendering

Pages that read the CMS render static. Reads only touch `cookies()` and `headers()` in Draft Mode, so visitors get the cached page. Same for `<cms.PreviewBanner />`.

To go static:

- Don't set `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`.
- Have `DATABASE_URL` at build time. No database at build? Keep `force-dynamic` on pages reading the CMS.
- Optional: prebuild dynamic routes. Without it a route renders on its first visit, then is cached.

```tsx
export const generateStaticParams = async () => (await cms.listSlugs('posts')).map((slug) => ({ slug }));
```

What to know:

- **Edits go live.** Each save or delete revalidates `'/'` (layout) by default. Publish refreshes the page and lists; unpublish gives a 404. Narrow it with the `revalidate` option.
- **Drafts preview fine** on static routes. Leave `dynamicParams` at its default: `listSlugs` returns published slugs only, so `dynamicParams = false` would 404 a draft.
- **Keep request APIs off public pages.** `cms.isAdmin()`, `cookies()`, `headers()` and `searchParams` make that page dynamic.
- `/admin` and the API route are always dynamic.

## Caching

Out of the box, a read is de-duplicated within one request only. Every request that reads content queries the database. Turn on `cache` (recommended) to keep published reads between requests:

```ts
createCms(config, { cache: true }); // or { revalidate: 600 }
```

- Covers `getSingleton`, `getEntry`, `getEntries`, `listEntries` and `listSlugs`. Each save, publish, unpublish or delete drops what was cached for that collection, so edits show at once.
- Your own `revalidate` option does not stop that. It only replaces the default `revalidatePath`.
- Draft Mode, `all: true` and the admin always read fresh data.
- `revalidate` (seconds, default 3600) is the longest a read lives. Content written outside the CMS (`db:import`, `sync`, SQL, another app) does not drop the cache, so it shows up after this time. Lower it if you write that way often.
- Next stores each cached value up to about 2 MB. A longer list is read from the database each time. Use `limit`, or `getEntries`, on huge collections.
- Built on Next's `unstable_cache`, which Next replaced with `use cache`. On an app with `cacheComponents` on, test it before relying on it.

## Stale values

A stored value that no longer fits its field (the config changed since it was saved) reads as the field's empty value, so a page never gets a value of the wrong kind. `next dev` logs a warning for each one. Editors settle it in the admin ([Changing fields](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/changing-fields.md)).

## `listEntries` options

| Option | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `orderBy` | Field, derived value, `'slug'`, `'createdAt'`, `'updatedAt'`. Default `'slug'`. Empties last. |
| `order` | `'asc'` or `'desc'` |
| `filter` | `(entry) => boolean` |
| `limit`, `offset` | Numbers |

Items have `createdAt` / `updatedAt` (`Date`; `null` for a never-saved draft in preview).

## `getEntries`

`getEntries(collection, slugs)`: several entries, one query. For `references` fields. Published only, in `slugs` order. Skips missing, unpublished and repeated slugs.

## Live preview

Render `<cms.PreviewBanner />` in your site layout. Only previewing editors see it; pages stay static for everyone else.

Saving revalidates the whole site (`revalidatePath('/', 'layout')`). Change it with `revalidate`.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/search.md -->

# Search

Search the published content from your own code, an agent or a RAG pipeline. Off by default.

The package cuts each published entry into passages and keeps an **index** up to date. The index is yours, like [image storage](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/image-storage.md): Postgres, Mongo, Convex, Algolia, Pinecone… with or without embeddings. The package ships no index and no embedding code, so it never ties you to a database or a provider. Below are working examples to copy.

```ts filename="src/mnml/index.ts"
export const cms = createCms(config, {
  storage: myStorage, // any storage
  auth: { password: process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD, secret: process.env.ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET },
  search: { index: myIndex },
});
```

```ts
const hits = await cms.search('how do refunds work', { collections: ['posts'], limit: 5 });
// [{ key, slug, title, url, field, snippet, text, score }]
```

- Each hit is the best passage of one entry, best first.
- `text` is the whole passage (up to about 1,600 characters). Hand it to a model as is.
- `snippet` is a short piece around the match, for a results page.
- `slug` is `null` for a singleton. `url` is the page on your site, or `null`.
- `score`: higher is better. Compare scores only inside one result list.
- Drafts are never indexed or returned. Unpublished and deleted entries drop out.

## The index

A `SearchIndex` has three methods and one optional one:

```ts
import type { SearchIndex } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/next';

export const myIndex: SearchIndex = {
  // Replace everything stored for this entry.
  async put({ id, key, slug, title, url, chunks }) {
    // id: 'posts/hello' ('settings/' for a singleton). chunks: [{ field, idx, text, hash }]
  },
  // The entry was unpublished or deleted.
  async remove(id) {},
  // The best passages, best first: [{ key, slug, title, url, field, text, score }]
  async query(q, { collections, limit }) {
    return [];
  },
  // Optional: drop every entry whose id is not in `live` (used by reindex).
  async prune(live) {},
};
```

- `put` gets only published entries, never drafts.
- Make `put` one statement or transaction where you can: delete what the entry no longer has and write the rest together. Then two saves of one entry cannot leave half of each.
- Each chunk has a `hash`. Skip passages whose hash you already hold, so unchanged text is not embedded again.
- `query` may return several passages of one entry. The package keeps the best of each, so it asks for about three times as many passages as results.
- The index can live in another system from the entries. That is the normal case for Algolia and Typesense.

Helpers, exported from `@n3wtou/mnml-cms/next` and `/sync`:

- `searchEntry(config, key, slug, data)`: the id, title, link and passages of one entry, if you want to feed an index yourself.
- `fuseMatches([wordMatches, vectorMatches])`: merges ranked lists (reciprocal rank fusion), for hybrid search.

## Example: Postgres full-text

Words only, with stemming and ranking. No extension, no API key. This is the whole adapter; the repo's example has it as [`postgres-search.ts`](https://github.com/mbuguanewton/mnml-cms/blob/main/example/src/mnml/postgres-search.ts).

```sql
create table if not exists mnml_chunks (
  entry text not null,
  idx int not null,
  key text not null,
  slug text,
  title text not null,
  url text,
  field text not null,
  text text not null,
  tsv tsvector generated always as (to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || text)) stored,
  primary key (entry, idx)
);
create index if not exists mnml_chunks_tsv_idx on mnml_chunks using gin (tsv);
```

```ts filename="src/mnml/postgres-search.ts"
import { neon } from '@neondatabase/serverless';
import type { SearchIndex, SearchMatch } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/sync';

export function postgresSearch(url: string | undefined): SearchIndex {
  // Created when first used, so a build without DATABASE_URL still works.
  const db = () => neon(url ?? '');
  return {
    async put({ id, key, slug, title, url, chunks }) {
      // Upsert the passages and delete the ones past the end, in one statement.
      await db()`
        with up as (
          insert into mnml_chunks (entry, idx, key, slug, title, url, field, text)
          select ${id}, i, ${key}, ${slug}, ${title}, ${url}, f, t
          from unnest(${chunks.map((c) => c.idx)}::int[], ${chunks.map((c) => c.field)}::text[], ${chunks.map((c) => c.text)}::text[]) as c(i, f, t)
          on conflict (entry, idx) do update set key = excluded.key, slug = excluded.slug, title = excluded.title, url = excluded.url, field = excluded.field, text = excluded.text
        )
        delete from mnml_chunks where entry = ${id} and idx >= ${chunks.length}`;
    },
    async remove(id) {
      await db()`delete from mnml_chunks where entry = ${id}`;
    },
    async prune(live) {
      await db()`delete from mnml_chunks where entry <> all(${live})`;
    },
    async query(q, { collections, limit }) {
      // Any word matches; passages with more of them rank higher.
      const words = (q.match(/[\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu) ?? []).join(' or ');
      const rows = await db()`
        select key, slug, title, url, field, text, ts_rank_cd(tsv, query) as score
        from mnml_chunks, websearch_to_tsquery('english', ${words}) as query
        where tsv @@ query and (${collections ?? null}::text[] is null or key = any(${collections ?? null}))
        order by score desc limit ${limit}`;
      return rows.map((r) => ({ ...(r as SearchMatch), score: Number(r.score) }));
    },
  };
}
```

Any Postgres client works the same way: swap Neon's `sql` for your own.

## Example: search by meaning (pgvector)

[`pgvector-search.ts`](https://github.com/mbuguanewton/mnml-cms/blob/main/example/src/mnml/pgvector-search.ts) wraps the Postgres example for the words, keeps vectors in a second table, and merges both lists with `fuseMatches`. Embedding is a function you pass:

```ts
search: { index: pgvectorSearch({ url: process.env.DATABASE_URL, embed: geminiEmbed(), model: 'gemini-embedding-001' }) },
```

The file has `openaiEmbed()` and `geminiEmbed()`, both small `fetch` calls. Gemini is tested against the real API, including a Spanish query finding English text. Voyage, Cohere or a local model work the same.

1. `create extension if not exists vector;` and the vectors table: [`search-vectors.sql`](https://github.com/mbuguanewton/mnml-cms/blob/main/example/scripts/search-vectors.sql). Neon, Supabase and most hosts have pgvector.
2. `cms.search.reindex()`. Run it again when you change the model: the model is stored with each vector, so old and new vectors are never mixed.

Good to know:

- Vector search always returns the nearest entries, even for a query with no real match. Cut by `score` or show fewer results if that matters.
- Embed in `put` after the words are stored, so a provider outage never makes new content unsearchable.
- Embedding calls the network, so that `put` is not one statement. If two saves of one entry overlap, `reindex()` repairs it.
- If embedding the query fails, answer from the words only.

## Other databases

The pieces are the same everywhere: store passages on `put`, delete them on `remove`, search them on `query`.

- **MongoDB:** an Atlas Search index (text) and Atlas Vector Search on a collection of passages. `put`: delete the entry's passages and insert the new ones. `query`: `$search` and/or `$vectorSearch`.
- **Convex:** a table of passages with a search index and a vector index. `put` and `remove` call mutations, `query` calls a query function.
- **Firebase:** Firestore has no full-text or vector search. Use Typesense, Algolia, Meilisearch or Vertex AI Vector Search as the index.
- **Hosted vector databases** (Pinecone, Turbopuffer, Qdrant): `put` upserts vectors with the passage as metadata, `remove` deletes by entry, `query` embeds and searches.

These are not shipped as packages: your database, your embeddings, your adapter.

## Reindex

`reindex()` puts every published entry into the index, then calls `prune`. Run it:

- after turning `search` on for a site with content,
- after [moving content](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/moving-content.md) between databases,
- after changing your embedding model or index.

```ts
const { entries, chunks, failed } = await cms.search.reindex();
```

One entry that fails (say, your embedding provider rejects it) does not stop the rest. It is listed in `failed` as `{ key, slug, message }`, and its old passages are kept. Run `reindex()` again to retry.

Scripts and cron jobs can run it without Next.js, with the same storage and index as `createCms`:

```ts filename="scripts/reindex.ts"
import { createSearch, drizzleStorage, neonDatabase } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/sync';
import config from '../mnml.config';
import { postgresSearch } from '../src/mnml/postgres-search';

const url = process.env.DATABASE_URL;
const { failed } = await createSearch(config, { storage: drizzleStorage(neonDatabase(url)), index: postgresSearch(url) }).reindex();
if (failed.length) process.exitCode = 1;
```

## What gets indexed

- Text, textarea, rich text and tags fields, also inside groups, lists and blocks.
- Not the title field (every passage carries the entry's title instead), numbers, dates, links, images, selects or references.
- Long fields are split at paragraphs and sentences into passages of about 400 tokens.

## For agents

With the [MCP server](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/agents.md) on, agents get a `search_content` tool (scope `read`). It returns the best passages with their entry, field, link and text, limited to the collections the token can read. The older `search` tool stays: it finds exact text in the latest versions, drafts included, for editing.

## Public route

```ts
search: { index: myIndex, route: ['posts', 'pages'] },
```

Turns on `GET <apiPath>/search?q=…&collections=posts&limit=10` (JSON `{ ok, results }`). It answers anyone, with the full text of each passage, so it is off by default.

- `route: true` searches every collection and singleton. A list of keys limits it to those. Use the list: a collection you publish but never show on the site would otherwise be searchable.
- `cms.search()` in your own code is never limited by the list.
- `q` up to 200 characters. `limit` up to 20. Only published content.
- 30 searches a minute for each client and 300 in all. Over that: `429` with `Retry-After`.
- The counts are kept in memory on each server, and clients are told apart by `x-forwarded-for`. Treat it as a guard, not a quota. If the index costs money per search, also limit the route at your host or CDN.

## Options

| Option | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | required | Your `SearchIndex`. |
| `route` | `false` | Turns on the public route: `true` (everything) or a list of collection keys. |

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/assistant.md -->

# Assistant

A chat panel in the admin. A button at the bottom right opens it. Off by default.

The assistant knows the page the editor has open: the fields and their current values. Editors can:

- **Ask about the content.** "Which posts mention refunds?" It searches the published content and answers from it.
- **Ask it to write.** "Write a summary", "Suggest a better title", "Fill in the empty fields". What it writes goes into the form as an **unsaved edit**. The editor reads it, changes it or presses **Undo**, then saves or publishes as usual.

The assistant can read content. It cannot save, publish, unpublish or delete anything. Only the editor does that.

## Turn it on

Install the [AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev) (`ai`). The package has no provider code of its own, and sites that don't use the assistant never load it.

```sh
npm i ai
```

Then pass an assistant to `createCms`. The easiest model is an [AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway) id: no provider package, one key.

```ts filename="src/mnml/index.ts"
import { assistant } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/ai';

export const cms = createCms(config, {
  database: neonDatabase(process.env.DATABASE_URL),
  auth: { password: process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD, secret: process.env.ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET },
  ai: assistant({ model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5' }),
});
```

Set `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` in `.env.local`. On Vercel no key is needed: it signs in by itself. Model ids are `provider/model`, as listed in the [Gateway's model list](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models). The Gateway also gives you fallbacks, spend budgets and logs, so you don't build those.

The key stays on the server. The browser only talks to `<apiPath>/ai/chat`.

For answers about the whole site, turn on [search](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/search.md) too. Without it, the assistant can still list and read entries and search by keyword, but not by meaning.

Replies are shown as Markdown by a small built-in renderer. To use your own (for tables or code highlighting), give the `Markdown` slot of the [custom admin UI](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/custom-admin-ui.md) a component.

## Choosing a model

`model` is a Gateway id string, or any AI SDK model. To go to a provider directly, install its package:

```ts
import { google } from '@ai-sdk/google'; // npm i @ai-sdk/google, key in GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY

ai: assistant({ model: google('gemini-2.5-flash') }),
```

`@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `@ai-sdk/openai` and many more work the same way, and so does any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (a local model, for example). See the [AI SDK providers](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers).

## Name and tone

Give it a name and a voice. The name is what the button and the panel are called, and what the model calls itself. The tone is how it answers and how it writes into fields.

```ts
ai: assistant({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5',
  name: 'Scribe', // default 'Assistant'
  tone: 'Friendly and concise. Plain words, no jargon.',
}),
```

Write the tone in your own words: "Formal, British spelling", "Short sentences, no exclamation marks". It applies to the answers and to the text the assistant puts in fields.

## Your own tools

Give the assistant tools of your own, made with `tool()` from `ai`: a price from your shop API, stock from your warehouse, a style guide.

```ts
import { tool } from 'ai';
import { z } from 'zod';

ai: assistant({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5',
  tools: {
    productPrice: tool({
      description: 'Current price of a product from our shop API',
      inputSchema: z.object({ sku: z.string() }),
      execute: async ({ sku }) => (await fetch(`https://shop.example.com/api/${sku}`)).json(),
    }),
  },
}),
```

The panel shows "Using productPrice…" while a tool runs. A tool that throws doesn't stop the answer: the model is told it failed.

A function gets the open page, so a tool can exist only where it belongs:

```ts
tools: ({ page }) => (page.key === 'posts' ? { productPrice } : {}),
```

`page` is `{ key, slug }` of the entry the editor has open, or empty on other screens. A tool can use your `cms` too (`cms.getEntry`, `cms.search`); write the `execute` return type out when you do, because `cms` is the value being built.

- Your tools run on your server for signed-in editors only, and can do whatever your code does, including writes. Keep them to reading. The assistant's own way to change content is the form, and the editor reviews that.
- A tool can't have the name of a built-in one (`get_schema`, `list_entries`, `get_entry`, `search`, `search_content`, `fill_field`, `fill_entry`).
- A tool can't see or change the form. Only `fill_field` and `fill_entry` do, and what they put in is checked first.

## The CMS's tools in your own code

`cms.tools()` returns read tools in the AI SDK's format, so you can give an agent or a RAG pipeline of your own access to the content:

```ts
import { streamText } from 'ai';

const result = streamText({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5',
  tools: { ...cms.tools(), productPrice },
  prompt: 'Which posts talk about refunds?',
});
```

By default they see the **published** content only: search (when [`search`](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/search.md) is on), the schema, and published list and get. That is safe behind a public chatbot. They cannot write. `cms.tools({ collections: ['posts'] })` limits what they can see.

`cms.tools({ drafts: true })` adds drafts and unpublished edits, which is what the admin's assistant sees. Use it only for signed-in editors, never in a public route.

## Earlier chats

**New chat** starts a fresh conversation. The ones before stay: a **History** button in the panel lists the earlier chats of the page the editor has open, newest first, and opens one to read or carry on in. An entry only sees its own chats, and the dashboard and list screens share one list.

By default the chats are kept in the editor's browser (`localStorage`):

- They are not on your server or in your database, and not shared between editors or devices.
- Each answer is kept as a **turn**: the question, the answer and which fields were filled. The form's values are never stored.
- The last 12 chats of each page are kept, within about 150,000 characters. When there are more, the oldest chat goes, with all its turns.
- **Delete this chat**, in the History menu, removes one yourself.
- A reopened chat's old fills have no **Undo**, because the form has moved on.
- A chat belongs to the page it was had on. When a new entry is saved and gets its address, the panel starts fresh on the new page and the earlier chat stays in History under the old one.
- The chats stay in the browser after the editor signs out. On a shared computer, clear the site's data.

To keep them in your own database, and to keep a record of what the assistant did, give `assistant()` a [`store`](#keeping-a-record).

## Keeping a record

To see what the assistant did over time (what it was asked, which tools it used, what it changed in the forms, what it cost), keep every turn in your own database. You write a small store for your database, like [search](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/search.md)'s index. The package has no database code.

```ts
ai: assistant({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5',
  store: {
    // Append one row per question. Runs after the answer is sent, so it never slows it.
    async record(turn, { request }) {
      await db.insert(assistantTurns).values({ ...turn, by: (await sessionOf(request))?.user.id });
    },
    // Optional: read the History menu from your table instead of the browser.
    async turns(page) {
      return db.select().from(assistantTurns).where(eq(assistantTurns.page, page)).orderBy(desc(assistantTurns.at)).limit(300);
    },
  },
}),
```

A **turn** is one question and its answer:

| Field | |
| --- | --- |
| `chatId`, `page`, `at` | The chat it belongs to, the page (`posts/hello`, `settings/` for a singleton, or `site`), and when the answer finished. |
| `question`, `answer` | What was asked and said. |
| `status` | `done`, `stopped` (the editor stopped it, or it ran out of steps) or `error`. |
| `tools` | Every tool it called, with its input (cut when long): searches, reads, your own tools. |
| `fills` | What it put in the form: `fields`, `before` and `after` values, and `dropped` (what was left out, and why). |
| `model`, `usage`, `durationMs` | The model, tokens used, and how long it took. |

- **Append only.** Never update or delete these rows: it is the record. That is why the History menu has no Delete when it reads from your table.
- **Who asked.** `record` and `turns` get the editor's `Request`. The package doesn't know your login, but your code does: read your session there and fill a `by` column.
- **Failures.** A failed `record` is logged and never shown. A failed `turns` shows an empty list.
- **Privacy.** `before` and `after` can hold your content. They go only to your database. Keep what you need and set a retention for the table.
- **`record` is required, `turns` is optional.** With `record` alone you keep the audit trail and the History menu stays in the browser.
- Use parameterised queries: the `page` comes from the request. The package checks and caps what `turns` returns (300 turns, newest first).

`groupTurns(turns)`, from `@n3wtou/mnml-cms/ai`, puts turns back into chats (newest first, each with its messages), if you want a history page of your own.

### Example: Postgres

`example/src/mnml/postgres-assistant-store.ts` in the repo is a store for Postgres (Neon's `sql` tag), with the table in `example/scripts/assistant.sql` and `pnpm db:assistant` to create it:

```sql
create table if not exists mnml_assistant_turns (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  chat_id text not null,
  page text not null,
  at timestamptz not null,
  question text not null,
  answer text not null,
  status text not null,
  model text,
  tools jsonb,
  fills jsonb,
  usage jsonb,
  duration_ms int,
  by text
);
create index if not exists mnml_assistant_turns_page_idx on mnml_assistant_turns (page, at desc);
create index if not exists mnml_assistant_turns_chat_idx on mnml_assistant_turns (chat_id);
```

## What the model can do

| It can | Through |
| --- | --- |
| Read the schema, list entries, read an entry | the same read tools as the [MCP server](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/agents.md) |
| Search the published content by meaning | `search_content` (needs [`search`](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/search.md)) |
| Search by keyword, drafts included | `search` |
| Put values in the open entry | `fill_field` and `fill_entry` |
| Anything you add | your own [tools](#your-own-tools) |

The assistant's own tools can't save, publish or delete. Tools you add can do what your code does, so keep them to reading.

Before values reach the form, the server checks each field the way a save does. Rich text can be Markdown. A value that does not fit its field, or a field that does not exist, is left out, and the model is told which and why so it can try again. The panel lists what was left out.

## Limits and safety

- Only signed-in editors can use it: `POST <apiPath>/ai/chat` returns 401 otherwise, and 404 when `ai` is off. `GET <apiPath>/ai/chats?page=` (only with a `store` that has `turns`) is the same.
- 20 questions a minute for each client, per server instance. This is a guard, not a budget: for a real spend cap use the AI Gateway's budgets, or your provider's.
- A request carries at most 30 messages and 60,000 characters. The form's values sent to the model are cut at 40,000 characters.
- Content is data, not instructions: the model is told never to follow instructions it finds in content. Even if it did, it can only fill the open form. The editor sees the result before anything is saved.
- Filled values are **unsaved edits** in the form. A collection entry that already exists autosaves as a draft like any other edit, and the live version only changes when the editor publishes.
- A model that fails does not leak its error to the browser. The detail goes to the server log.

## Options

The options of `assistant()`:

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `model` | A Gateway id string or an AI SDK model. Required. |
| `tools` | Your own tools, as an object or a function of the open page. |
| `maxSteps` | Most model turns for one question. Default 6. |
| `store` | Where the record of turns goes, in your database ([Keeping a record](#keeping-a-record)). Default: none, and the panel keeps its chats in the browser. |
| `name` | What the panel and button are called, and what the model calls itself. Default `Assistant`. Up to 40 characters. |
| `tone` | How it writes and answers, in your words. Up to 300 characters. |

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/drafts-and-publishing.md -->

# Drafts and publishing

A collection entry is draft or published. The admin's dot:

- **Green:** published
- **Grey:** draft
- **Orange over green:** published, with unpublished changes

## Collection list

- 25 entries a page, with Previous / Next.
- The search box filters by title or slug as you type (Enter without JavaScript).
- **Columns** chooses what the table shows. **Filters** narrows the list. **Column headers** sort it. **Checkboxes** select rows for bulk actions.
- Page, search, filters and sort live in the URL (`?q=…&status=draft&f.category=news&sort=f.date&dir=desc&page=2`), so links and the back button work.

### Filters

The Filters button opens a panel with one filter per field that can be filtered, in config order. Status (Draft, Changes, Published) is always first. A chip under the button shows each set filter, and **Clear filters** removes them all. Changing a filter starts again at page 1. Filters need JavaScript. The search box doesn't.

| Field | Filter |
| --- | --- |
| `select` | A dropdown of its options (with their labels). |
| `boolean` | Any, Yes or No. No also matches entries where it was never set. |
| `date`, `datetime` | From and to, both included. Entries without a date never match. A `datetime` is compared by its UTC day. |
| `number` | Min and max. Entries without a number never match. |
| `reference` | A dropdown of the target collection's published entries. |

Pick which filters show with `filters` on the collection. It takes field names, shown in that order. `filters: false` hides the whole control, status too.

```ts
posts: collection({
  label: 'Posts',
  titleField: 'title',
  basePath: '/blog',
  filters: ['category', 'featured', 'date'], // default: every filterable field
  fields: {
    title: fields.text('Title'),
    category: fields.select('Category', ['news', 'guide'] as const),
    featured: fields.boolean('Featured'),
    date: fields.date('Date'),
  },
});
```

A name that isn't a field, or is a field type that can't be filtered (`text`, `richtext`, `image`, `tags`, `references`, groups, blocks, arrays), throws when the config loads, and TypeScript flags a misspelt name.

### Columns and sorting

The table shows the title, Slug, Status and the first `date` field. Click a header to sort ascending, again for descending, a third time for the default order (newest `date` first). The header's arrow and `aria-sort` show the state.

- Text sorts without regard to case, numbers as numbers, dates as dates.
- A `select` sorts by its label, a `reference` by the target's title, a `boolean` with No first, Status as Draft, Changes, Published.
- Empty values come last in both directions. Equal values keep their order.

`columns` on the collection chooses the field columns, in order. The first is the link to the entry, then come Slug and Status, then the rest. Every column sorts. Shown: `text`, `url`, `date`, `datetime`, `number`, `boolean`, `select` and `reference`.

```ts
columns: ['title', 'category', 'date', 'featured'],
```

### Choosing columns

The **Columns** button opens a menu with a check mark beside each column: Slug, Status and every field that can be shown. Tick one to show it, untick to hide it; the menu stays open while you do. The first column (the link to the entry) is always shown. **Reset to default** goes back to the collection's `columns` (or the standard table).

The choice is kept per collection in this browser, in a cookie named `mnml_cols_<collection>` (set on the admin path, for a year; the server reads it, so the table renders right at once). Nothing is stored in the database, and other editors and browsers keep their own. Columns show in the menu's order: the ones the table shows by default first, then the other fields in config order. A sort on a column you hide is dropped.

**Filters follow the columns once you have chosen them.** A field's filter shows only while its column does, and Status only while the Status column does. Hide Category and its filter goes; show it again and it returns. A filter that was set on a hidden column is ignored (not applied), like a sort, and comes back with the column. Before you choose columns, every filter shows as configured; **Reset to default** returns to that. With no filters left (only the first column showing) the Filters button is hidden. `columnChoices: false` turns this off along with the choice.

`columnChoices` on the collection limits what the menu offers, besides Slug and Status. It takes field names, or `false` for no Columns button (the table then always shows `columns` or the default). A name that isn't a field, or isn't one of the shown types, throws when the config loads.

```ts
columnChoices: ['category', 'date', 'featured'], // default: every field that can be a column
```

### Bulk actions

A checkbox on each row (and one in the header for the whole page) selects entries. A bar appears at the bottom with the actions that apply:

| Action | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Publish** | Makes drafts, and entries with unpublished changes, live. Asks for nothing. |
| **Unpublish** | Takes live entries off the site; their content becomes a draft. Asks first. |
| **Delete** | Deletes the entries. Asks first, and says how many are published. |

A button is disabled when it would do nothing to the selection (Publish when everything is live). Each entry is handled like a single save: validated, and `revalidate` / `onChange` run for it. An entry that can't be published (a required field is empty) is reported and left alone; the rest still go through. Entries already in the target state are skipped. Up to 100 at a time. A new search, filter, sort or page starts with nothing selected.

#### Your own actions

`listActions` in `createCms` adds buttons to the bar for a collection. Each runs once per selected entry, on the server. It's a server option because `mnml.config.ts` is plain data.

```ts
export const cms = createCms(config, {
  // …
  listActions: {
    posts: [
      {
        name: 'refresh', // unique in the collection; not publish, unpublish or delete
        label: 'Refresh on site',
        // danger: true,                    // red button
        // confirm: 'Rebuilds each page.',  // asks first (the admin adds how many)
        run: ({ key, slug, entry }) => revalidatePath(`/posts/${slug}`), // entry: its latest data
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

Throw an error to mark that entry as failed; the message is shown. A site action applies to every selected entry, whatever its status.

## Autosave

Edits to an existing entry save ~1.5 s after typing stops ("Saving…", then "Saved"). No save button for drafts.

| Action | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Publish** | Draft becomes live. |
| **Discard changes** (⋮) | Drops unpublished changes, back to live. |
| **Unpublish** (⋮) | Takes it off the site. Content becomes a draft. |

A new entry: **Create draft** stores it, **Publish** puts it live. Autosaves after that.

### Only valid data is saved

- Invalid or empty required field: header says "Not saved: \<field\>: \<problem\>".
- Unsaved edits live in the browser only. Leaving warns first.
- So Publish never fails on a stored draft.

### Someone else edited it

Changed since you opened it? Autosave stops and asks you to reload. Never overwrites.

## On your site

Public readers (`listEntries`, `getEntry`, `getEntries`, `listSlugs`) return published entries only. A draft is a 404.

Editors see their draft in live preview, and anywhere on the site while Draft Mode is on for that entry (until "Exit preview").

## Singletons

Live by default: Save publishes. `drafts: true` gives autosave, Publish and Discard changes.

```ts
settings: singleton({ label: 'Settings', drafts: true, fields: { /* … */ } }),
```

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/changing-fields.md -->

# Changing fields

Entries outlive the config. Change a field (rich text to text, a `select` option removed, text to date) and saved entries still hold values of the old kind.

## In the admin

Open an entry. A field whose stored value no longer fits shows a card instead of its input:

- **Stored**: the old value. Rich text shows as its words, anything else as text or JSON.
- **As a text field** (the new kind): a suggested value, when there is a sensible one. Edit it before you accept. What you type is checked as that kind of value (a date must be a date).
- **What is lost**: a line under the suggestion when converting drops something, e.g. "Lost: 1 heading, a list" (rich text to text), "The time of day is dropped" (date and time to date).
- **Use this**: puts the suggestion (as edited) into the field. Only shown when there is one.
- **Remove**: drops the old value. The card is replaced by the normal, empty field. Always shown.

A banner at the top counts the fields and links to each card.

- Nothing is saved until every card is settled. Autosave waits ("Resolve 2 fields first") and Publish is off. The old content can't be overwritten by accident.
- Use this and Remove change the form only. The old value stays in the database until you save.
- Cards also show inside groups, array items and blocks. The first row with a card opens by itself. Other rows with one are marked "Needs attention", and the banner links open them. A card moves with its row when you reorder, and goes when you remove the row.
- It works for the published version, unpublished changes and a draft. The banner names which one you are editing.
- Empty values (`null`, `''`, `[]`) are fixed without asking: nothing is lost.
- A field hidden by `showIf` is fixed without asking too. Saving does the same.

## What Use this can convert

| Stored | New field | Becomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rich text | `text`, `textarea` | Plain text. Blank line between blocks. `text` joins them on one line. |
| Text | `richtext` | A paragraph for each line |
| Text, number | `number` | The number (`"1,250"` is 1250) |
| `yes` `no` `true` `false` `1` `0` `on` `off` | `boolean` | `true` or `false` |
| Text | `select` | The option with that value or label, ignoring case |
| Text, number (milliseconds) | `date`, `datetime` | The date, or the UTC time |
| Text | `url` | A link (`example.com` gets `https://`) |
| Text with commas, `;` or lines | `tags`, `references` | A list |
| Text, number | `reference` | That text, if it is one word |

Everything else has no suggestion: `image`, `array`, `group`, `blocks`, objects. Use Remove.

## On the site

Readers (`getEntry`, `listEntries`, `getEntries`, `getSingleton`) never pass a value that doesn't fit its field. It reads as the field's empty value, and `next dev` logs one warning for each entry and field. A stale value can't break a page for visitors.

- The stored data is not changed. Only the admin's Save changes it.
- Values that were always valid read as before.
- The admin, the MCP server and `sync` see what is stored.

Prefer to migrate on purpose? Write a script with `@n3wtou/mnml-cms/sync` ([Moving content](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/moving-content.md)).

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/moving-content.md -->

# Moving content between databases

Seed prod from dev, or pull prod back into dev. `@n3wtou/mnml-cms/sync` exports content to JSON, compares a file with a database, and writes the difference. It runs in a plain script, no Next.js.

The example's `scripts/content.ts`:

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm db:export` | `DATABASE_URL` to `mnml-content.json` |
| `pnpm db:import mnml-content.json --mode add` | Dry run: file into `DATABASE_URL` |
| `pnpm db:sync --from DATABASE_URL --to PROD_DATABASE_URL --mode add --apply --yes` | One database into another |
| `pnpm db:sync --from-env-file .env.local --to-env-file .env.production --mode add --apply --yes` | Same, URLs read from files |

## Choosing the databases

- `--env`, `--from`, `--to`: name an env var holding a database URL. URLs stay out of shell history.
- `--env-file`, `--from-env-file`, `--to-env-file`: read the var from a file. Default var `DATABASE_URL`. The file is only read, never loaded into the env.
- A `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` in the target's file powers the missing-image check.

## Modes

| `--mode` | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `add` | Adds missing entries. Leaves existing ones. |
| `overwrite` | Also replaces entries that differ. |
| `replace` | Target matches the file. Deletes entries not in it. |

## Safety

- Dry run until `--apply`.
- A database not on localhost also needs `--yes`.
- Target content is backed up to `.mnml-backups/` first. Undo: `db:import <backup> --mode replace`.
- Entries are checked against your config. Any misfit: nothing is written.
- Source and target can't be the same.
- Running twice is safe.
- Not atomic (Neon HTTP has no transactions). Stopped halfway? Run again.

## What moves

| Moves | Doesn't |
| --- | --- |
| Collections and singletons in the config | Sign-in state |
| Their autosaved drafts | Preview copies |
| | **Uploaded images** |

- The script lists images the target's storage lacks. Copy those files yourself.
- `createdAt` / `updatedAt` are set when written.

## In your own scripts

Exported: `exportContent`, `planImport`, `applyImport`, `describePlan`, `missingMedia`. Connect with `drizzleStorage` or `neonDatabase`.

## Markdown content

`markdownToRichText` turns Markdown (a blog export, another CMS) into Tiptap JSON for a `richtext` field.

```ts
import { markdownToRichText, richTextToMarkdown } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/sync';

const content = markdownToRichText(post.body); // throws on tables and raw HTML
const { markdown, lossy } = richTextToMarkdown(entry.content); // lossy: some nodes became <!-- mnml:<type> -->
```

## Rehosting images

Images from another CMS live on its CDN (e.g. `cdn.sanity.io`). `mediaImporter` copies them into this site's storage and returns the URL for an `image` field.

```ts
import { mediaImporter, vercelBlobMedia } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/sync';

const importImage = mediaImporter(vercelBlobMedia()); // pass `apiPath` if it isn't /api/mnml
const { url } = await importImage('https://cdn.sanity.io/images/…/photo.jpg');
await storage.upsert('posts', slug, { …post, cover: { url, alt } }, 'published');
```

- Use the site's storage.
- Each source URL is stored once (file named after its hash). Later runs find it via `list()` and skip the download. Both built-in storages have `list()`; without it, repeats are only skipped within one importer.
- Accepts `https://` JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF up to 4 MB (`maxBytes` to raise). Else throws with the reason.
- `importRemoteMedia(url, storage)`: one image. Use one `mediaImporter` per run.
- Example script: `pnpm media:import <url…>`.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/editor.md -->

# Extending the editor

Add Tiptap extensions and toolbar buttons.

The editor (browser) and `<RichText>` (server) need the same extensions. So the config is a plain module both import (no `'use client'`):

```ts filename="src/mnml/editor.ts"
import { defineEditor, tools } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/editor';

export const editor = defineEditor({
  extensions: [], // added to the defaults (StarterKit + Image)
  tools: [tools.underline, tools.strike, tools.horizontalRule],
});
```

A client file wraps it for the admin:

```tsx filename="src/mnml/editor-client.tsx"
'use client';
import { editorProvider } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/admin';
import { editor } from './editor';
export const Editor = editorProvider(editor);
```

Then pass `editor: Editor` to `createCms`, and `editor={editor}` to every `<RichText>`:

```tsx
<RichText content={post.content} editor={editor} />
```

One config for every rich text field. Not per field: extensions can't travel in the schema sent to the admin.

## Ready-made tools

`tools.underline`, `tools.strike`, `tools.horizontalRule`: buttons for StarterKit features. No extension needed.

## Your own tools

A tool is an object:

```ts
type EditorTool = {
  name: string;
  label: string;
  icon: ReactNode;
  run: (editor: Editor, admin: ToolContext) => void;
  isActive?: (editor: Editor) => boolean;
  disabled?: (editor: Editor) => boolean;
  visible?: (editor: Editor) => boolean;
  context?: string;
  builtIn?: boolean;
  group?: 'format' | 'block' | 'insert';
};
```

| Property | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Unique. React key. |
| `label` | Tooltip, accessible name |
| `run` | On click. `admin` has `form()`, `confirm()`, `alert()` ([Nodes with a form](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/editor/nodes-with-a-form.md)). |
| `isActive` | Shows pressed |
| `disabled` | Disables |
| `visible` | Shown only when true |
| `context` | A node name: the tool shows in a mini toolbar above that node while the cursor is in it. |
| `builtIn` | Set on the package's tools |
| `group` | Toolbar group. None: own group at the end. |

`run`, `isActive`, `disabled`, `visible` get the live Tiptap editor.

## Toolbar groups

In order: undo/redo, text style menu (paragraph, headings, quote), `format` (bold, italic, code), `block` (lists), `insert` (link, image).

- `tools.underline`, `tools.strike`: `format`. `tools.horizontalRule`: `insert`.
- In each group, package tools (`tools.underline`, `tables.tools`…) first, then yours in listed order.

## Narrow fields and fullscreen

- Toolbar stays one row. Tools that don't fit move into a "More tools" (`…`) menu, from the end. Undo/redo and the text style menu always stay.
- Tools that can be on or off (with `isActive`) show checked in the menu.
- The editor box has a fixed height and scrolls. Drag its bottom-right corner to make it taller, like a textarea.
- The expand button (right end) opens the editor fullscreen. Escape or the button again closes it.
- Fullscreen header: entry title, field label, save status. Autosave keeps running.
- In fullscreen each tool shows its name next to its icon (and the text style button its current style). Tools that don't fit go into "More tools".

## Example: code blocks with syntax highlighting

Swap StarterKit's plain code block for [`CodeBlockLowlight`](https://tiptap.dev/docs/editor/extensions/nodes/code-block-lowlight) and add a button. To replace or remove a default extension, pass a function: it gets the defaults and returns the full list.

```tsx filename="src/mnml/editor.tsx"
import { defineEditor } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/editor';
import CodeBlockLowlight from '@tiptap/extension-code-block-lowlight';
import { common, createLowlight } from 'lowlight';
import { SquareCodeIcon } from 'lucide-react';

export const editor = defineEditor({
  extensions: (defaults) => [
    ...defaults.map((ext) => (ext.name === 'starterKit' ? ext.configure({ codeBlock: false }) : ext)),
    CodeBlockLowlight.configure({ lowlight: createLowlight(common) }),
  ],
  tools: [
    {
      name: 'codeBlock',
      label: 'Code block',
      group: 'block',
      icon: <SquareCodeIcon />,
      isActive: (e) => e.isActive('codeBlock'),
      run: (e) => e.chain().focus().toggleCodeBlock().run(),
    },
  ],
});
```

Highlighting shows in the editor only. `<RichText>` renders `<pre><code class="language-…">`: highlight it on the site yourself, or leave it plain.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/editor/tables.md -->

# Tables

Own entry point, so sites without tables skip the code. Spread its extensions and tools into the editor config:

```tsx filename="src/mnml/editor.tsx"
import { defineEditor } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/editor';
import { tables } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/table';

export const editor = defineEditor({
  extensions: [...tables.extensions],
  tools: [...tables.tools],
});
```

## In the editor

- **Insert table**: 3×3 with a header row. Before your own insert buttons.
- Cursor in a table: a mini toolbar above its right end. Add/delete row or column (at the cursor's cell), toggle header row, delete table. Hides when the cursor leaves.

## On your site

`<RichText editor={editor}>` renders a plain `<table>` (`<th>`, `<td>`, no widths). Style it with your prose.

## Your own floating tools

Give a tool `context: 'callout'`: it shows in the same mini toolbar above the nearest `callout` node while the cursor is inside.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/editor/nodes-with-a-form.md -->

# Nodes with a form

Some nodes need values: an embed's URL, a callout's tone. `tools.node()` makes a button that opens a form in a dialog, validates it like an entry, and inserts the node.

In the editor, the node is a card with a one-line preview. Double-click or press Edit to change it.

## 1. Define the node

Once, with its form fields, in a plain module the editor config and the site both import. `nodeAttributes(fields)` gives one attribute per field: starts empty, kept in HTML as `data-<name>`.

```ts filename="src/mnml/youtube.ts"
import { Node } from '@tiptap/core';
import { fields } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms';
import { nodeAttributes } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/editor';

export const youtubeFields = {
  url: fields.url('YouTube URL', { required: true }),
  title: fields.text('Title'),
};

export const YouTube = Node.create({
  name: 'youtube',
  group: 'block',
  atom: true, // a form node has no editable content of its own
  addAttributes: () => nodeAttributes(youtubeFields),
  parseHTML: () => [{ tag: 'div[data-youtube]' }],
  renderHTML: ({ HTMLAttributes }) => ['div', { 'data-youtube': '', ...HTMLAttributes }],
});
```

## 2. Add the button

```tsx filename="src/mnml/editor.tsx"
export const editor = defineEditor({
  extensions: [YouTube],
  tools: [
    tools.node({
      name: 'youtube',
      label: 'YouTube video',
      icon: <CirclePlayIcon />,
      group: 'insert',
      fields: youtubeFields,
      preview: (attrs) => attrs.url ?? '',
    }),
  ],
  components: { youtube: YouTubeEmbed },
});
```

- `name`: the node's name.
- `preview`: optional, the card's line.
- `components`: how `<RichText>` renders it on the site ([Custom node rendering](https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/editor/custom-rendering.md)).

## Form fields

- Allowed: `text`, `textarea`, `url`, `number`, `boolean`, `select`, `date`, `reference` (the slug). Values that fit node attributes.
- `required`, `help`, `showIf` work as in entries.

## Dialogs in any tool

`run` gets the editor and the dialogs `form`, `confirm`, `alert`. Any tool can use them.

```ts
run: async (editor, { form, confirm, alert }) => {
  const values = await form({ title: 'Callout', fields: calloutFields, submitLabel: 'Insert' }); // null if cancelled
  if (values) editor.chain().focus().insertContent({ type: 'callout', attrs: values }).run();
};
```

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/editor/linking-entries.md -->

# Linking entries from rich text

Link another entry from rich text, e.g. a card for another post.

- `tools.reference()`: a button that picks a published entry and inserts `{ type: name, attrs: { collection, slug } }`.
- `referenceNode({ name })`: a ready-made node for it.
- Editor shows a card with the entry's title. Double-click to pick another.

```tsx filename="src/mnml/editor.tsx"
import { defineEditor, referenceNode, tools } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/editor';

export const editor = defineEditor({
  extensions: [referenceNode({ name: 'blockLink' })],
  tools: [tools.reference({ name: 'blockLink', label: 'Link a post', icon: <FileSymlinkIcon />, collection: 'posts', group: 'insert' })],
});
```

## On your site

The node stores only the slug: your site loads the entries. `collectReferences(doc)` returns every link in the doc as `{ collection, slugs }[]`, repeats removed. Load them in one go, then render with a component:

```tsx
import { collectReferences, RichText } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/rich-text';

const slugs = collectReferences(post.content, ['blockLink']).find((r) => r.collection === 'posts')?.slugs ?? [];
const linked = new Map((await cms.getEntries('posts', slugs)).map((p) => [p.slug, p.entry]));

<RichText
  content={post.content}
  editor={editor}
  components={{ blockLink: ({ attrs }) => <PostCard slug={String(attrs.slug)} post={linked.get(String(attrs.slug))} /> }}
/>;
```

- A linked entry can disappear later (unpublished, deleted). Handle a missing one; the example renders nothing.
- Node forms (`tools.node`) can use a `reference` field too. It offers published entries.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/editor/custom-rendering.md -->

# Custom node rendering

`<RichText>` renders nodes with their extension's `renderHTML`. To use your own React component (an embed, highlighted code, a callout, an entry card), map the node's name to it.

The component gets `node` (Tiptap JSON), `attrs`, and `children` (rendered content; none for leaf nodes like images).

```tsx filename="src/components/code-block.tsx"
import type { RichTextNodeProps } from '@n3wtou/mnml-cms/editor';

export function CodeBlock({ attrs, children }: RichTextNodeProps) {
  return (
    <figure>
      <figcaption>{String(attrs.language ?? '')}</figcaption>
      <pre><code>{children}</code></pre>
    </figure>
  );
}
```

## For every `<RichText>`

In the editor config. Keys are node names: `codeBlock`, `image`, `blockquote`, yours…

```ts filename="src/mnml/editor.ts"
export const editor = defineEditor({
  components: { codeBlock: CodeBlock },
});
```

The admin loads this config in the browser, so these components ship to the client. Keep them plain.

## For one `<RichText>`

Pass `components`. Merged over the editor config's; wins for the same node.

```tsx
<RichText content={post.content} editor={editor} components={{ blockLink: PostCard }} />
```

Async server components go here, e.g. a card fetching the linked entry.

## Good to know

- Nodes without a component render as usual.
- Components for unknown nodes are ignored.

---

<!-- https://mnml-cms.vercel.app/options.md -->
